questions.topic: IAM: Roles, Service Accounts, and Organization Policies
questions.question: What is an IAM role?
options: A binding that attaches one principal to one resource in the hierarchy
A named collection of permissions that a binding grants to a principal
A constraint limiting which configurations a resource is allowed to have
An identity a workload authenticates as when it calls a Google Cloud API

questions.topic: IAM: Roles, Service Accounts, and Organization Policies
questions.question: What is a service account primarily used as?
options: A group that collects the human users who share one set of permissions
A key ring that holds the crypto keys one workload is allowed to use
A folder that gathers the projects one business unit is responsible for
A non-human identity that a workload authenticates and acts as

questions.topic: IAM: Roles, Service Accounts, and Organization Policies
questions.question: Why is permission to impersonate a service account sensitive?
options: The holder can exercise every access the impersonated identity already has
The holder gains the right to rename that account and its generated email
The holder can disable the organization policies attached to that project
The holder inherits the audit-log retention configured on that account

questions.topic: IAM: Roles, Service Accounts, and Organization Policies
questions.question: How does Organization Policy differ from an IAM allow grant?
options: It authorizes principals to act, whereas IAM describes resource shape
It applies only to a single project, whereas IAM inherits down the whole tree
It constrains the configurations resources may take, whatever IAM allows
It replaces the allow policy once a deny policy is attached to a folder

questions.topic: IAM: Roles, Service Accounts, and Organization Policies
questions.question: A Dataflow job reads one bucket and writes one dataset. What identity design best follows least privilege?
options: The project's default service account, holding Editor across the whole project
A downloaded key for a human account that already has both permissions
One shared platform identity reused by every pipeline in the organization
A dedicated service account with narrow roles on those two resources

questions.topic: IAM: Roles, Service Accounts, and Organization Policies
questions.question: A user has IAM permission to create a resource, but creation violates a location constraint. What should happen?
options: IAM overrides the constraint, since an explicit allow beats an inherited rule
Organization Policy rejects it, because the configuration itself is prohibited
The resource is created in the nearest allowed region without any warning
The request succeeds and the constraint is recorded as an audit exception

questions.topic: Encryption and Key Management: Google-Managed vs CMEK
questions.question: How is customer data at rest protected by default in Google Cloud?
options: It stays unencrypted until a customer attaches a Cloud KMS key to the service
Each service encrypts it with a key the customer uploads during provisioning
Google-owned and Google-managed keys encrypt it with no customer configuration
Cloud EKM holds the key material outside Google for each of the supported services

questions.topic: Encryption and Key Management: Google-Managed vs CMEK
questions.question: What does CMEK give the customer control over?
options: The lifecycle and policy of the KMS key a compatible service uses
The data encryption key the service generates for each individual object
The physical hardware module every one of Google's regions is built on
The algorithm each Google service applies to data while it is in transit

questions.topic: Encryption and Key Management: Google-Managed vs CMEK
questions.question: What is envelope encryption?
options: Encrypting the same data twice with two independent customer-managed keys
Encrypting each column with a key derived from that column's policy tag
Encrypting the key material itself and shipping it beside the ciphertext
Encrypting data with a data key, then wrapping that key with a key-encryption key

questions.topic: Encryption and Key Management: Google-Managed vs CMEK
questions.question: What normally happens during symmetric key rotation?
options: Every earlier version is destroyed once the new primary version is created
A new primary protects new writes while older versions still decrypt
The protected data is re-encrypted in place under the newest key version
The key ring moves to a new region so the rotation is geographically clean

questions.topic: Encryption and Key Management: Google-Managed vs CMEK
questions.question: Why must a team treat CMEK destruction as a high-risk operation?
options: Data protected by the destroyed version can become permanently unreadable
The service silently falls back to Google-managed keys for those resources
The destroyed version is retained for a year, so audits keep flagging it
The key ring's region changes, which breaks colocation with the resources

questions.topic: Encryption and Key Management: Google-Managed vs CMEK
questions.question: Which CMEK separation-of-duties design is strongest?
options: Grant every analyst both administer and use rights so nobody is ever blocked
Keep the key material in the pipeline's own repository beside its config
Split key administrators from the service identities that only encrypt and decrypt
Reuse one privileged human credential across all of the services involved

questions.topic: Cloud DLP: PII Detection and Masking
questions.question: What are Sensitive Data Protection detectors called?
options: Policy tags
InfoTypes
Aspect types
Entry types

questions.topic: Cloud DLP: PII Detection and Masking
questions.question: What does masking do?
options: It reduces a value's precision by placing it into a wider bucket
It substitutes a controlled token that a key holder can reverse
It shifts a date while preserving the intervals between records
It hides some or all characters of a detected sensitive value

questions.topic: Cloud DLP: PII Detection and Masking
questions.question: Why tune inspection configuration on representative data?
options: Because untuned scans cannot write findings to any output destination
Because likelihood thresholds are fixed once the first scan has completed
Because built-in detectors misfire on context, producing both error types
Because de-identification cannot run until a detector has been customized

questions.topic: Cloud DLP: PII Detection and Masking
questions.question: Which transformation can support controlled re-identification?
options: Reversible tokenization, under managed keys and authorization
Redaction, which removes the detected value from the record entirely
Bucketing, which lowers precision so an exact value cannot be recovered
Character masking, which leaves only the last few characters visible

questions.topic: Cloud DLP: PII Detection and Masking
questions.question: Why should inspection findings have restricted access?
options: Because a finding automatically grants its reader KMS decrypt permission
Because a finding names the location, type, and sometimes the context of sensitive data
Because findings count against the project's own data-processing quota
Because a finding is an organization policy that other teams inherit

questions.topic: Cloud DLP: PII Detection and Masking
questions.question: A deterministic token preserves joins across records. What residual risk should be evaluated?
options: The token cannot be joined across two tables that used different keys
The transform destroys analytical utility, so the join becomes meaningless
The token grows longer than the source value, inflating the stored bytes
Repeated tokens expose frequency and relationship patterns in the data

questions.topic: Data Residency and Sovereignty
questions.question: What does data residency primarily specify?
options: Where data is stored or processed, within a defined geographic boundary
Which laws and authorities govern the data once it has been stored
Which principals may read the data once it reaches its storage location
How long the data must be retained before its deletion policy applies

questions.topic: Data Residency and Sovereignty
questions.question: Why is data sovereignty broader than residency?
options: It fixes the exact region that every backup and every log export is written to
It measures the latency and egress cost of moving data across a boundary
It covers the laws, authorities, and operational controls, not just location
It replaces the residency requirement once a location constraint is set

questions.topic: Data Residency and Sovereignty
questions.question: What should a complete residency assessment trace?
options: The primary tables only, since derived copies inherit their location
Primary data, derivatives, logs, backups, metadata, keys, and access
The region label on each project, which every child resource inherits
The set of organization policies attached above the project's folder

questions.topic: Data Residency and Sovereignty
questions.question: What can a resource-location organization policy do?
options: Move data that already exists into one of the permitted locations
Verify that every external SaaS destination honors the same boundary
Override each product's own documented control-plane location behavior
Block creation of resources in locations it does not permit

questions.topic: Data Residency and Sovereignty
questions.question: A pipeline stores data in an approved region but sends full records to an external API elsewhere. What is the correct conclusion?
options: Residency holds, because the system of record never left the approved region
Residency holds, because the API call is processing rather than storage
The external call is part of the data path and belongs in the assessment
The location constraint will block the call once the policy is reapplied

questions.topic: Data Residency and Sovereignty
questions.question: Why should architects avoid claiming that data never leaves a country based only on a region setting?
options: Control planes, support access, logs, and recovery paths all need their own evidence
Region settings apply to storage only after the first backup has completed
A multi-region label always denotes a single country's set of data centers
Organization Policy disables backups whenever a location constraint applies

questions.topic: Project and Dataset Architecture for Governance
questions.question: What is a Google Cloud project commonly a boundary for?
options: Row-level and column-level access inside a single BigQuery table
The geographic location every dataset it contains must be created in
The set of encryption keys any other project is allowed to reference
APIs, quotas, billing association, many IAM grants, and lifecycle

questions.topic: Project and Dataset Architecture for Governance
questions.question: Why separate production and development projects?
options: It removes the need to attach any organization policy to either one
It limits blast radius and makes the policy differences explicit
It guarantees that development costs are billed at a discounted rate
It lets developers hold Owner in production without extra approvals

questions.topic: Project and Dataset Architecture for Governance
questions.question: Why separate raw, curated, and published BigQuery datasets?
options: They carry different owners, consumers, and access controls
A dataset is required before a table can be partitioned
Cross-dataset queries are blocked, which enforces the separation
Each dataset must sit in its own project to receive its own IAM

questions.topic: Project and Dataset Architecture for Governance
questions.question: Which statement about labels is correct?
options: Labels can carry a policy tag that restricts who reads a column
Labels are evaluated by IAM before an allow policy is applied
Labels help inventory and cost reporting but bound no access at all
Labels inherit from the folder and can override a project's own grants

questions.topic: Project and Dataset Architecture for Governance
questions.question: Analysts need de-identified output but not raw PII. What is the strongest straightforward design?
options: Grant analysts the raw dataset and rely on labels to mark sensitive tables
Grant the pipeline identity the raw dataset and analysts only the curated one
Place raw and curated tables in one dataset and share it through a listing
Grant analysts project-level roles so a single binding covers both datasets

questions.topic: Project and Dataset Architecture for Governance
questions.question: Which evidence best shows that a governance hierarchy is operationally useful?
options: Every access grant is reviewed and then applied by hand before it takes effect
The organization has reached the largest project count its quota allows
Owner, writer, readers, protections, and retirement are quickly answerable
One privileged identity is shared, so every environment behaves the same
